title: Pancit Bihon
description: The light, thin rice noodle version most people associate with Filipino Pancit. A birthday table staple symbolising long life, best served with a squeeze of calamansi.

method.instruction: Soak the bihon noodles in warm water for 10 minutes until softened, then drain and set aside.
Heat oil in a large wok over medium-high heat. Saute the garlic and onion until fragrant, then add the pork and chicken. Cook until browned.
Add the carrots, celery, and snow peas or green beans. Stir-fry for a few minutes until just tender, then remove the meat and vegetables from the wok and set aside to keep them crisp.
Pour the chicken broth, soy sauce, and fish sauce into the wok. Bring to a boil. Add the drained noodles and toss continuously until they absorb most of the liquid.
Return the cooked meat and vegetables to the wok. Add the shredded cabbage last and toss everything together until well combined and heated through.
Season with ground black pepper to taste. Transfer to a serving dish, top with chopped green onions, and serve with calamansi or lemon wedges on the side.

notes.title: Keep Vegetables Crisp
notes.content: Removing the vegetables from the wok before simmering the noodles prevents them from overcooking and going soggy.

notes.title: Noodle Soaking
notes.content: Do not oversoak the bihon — 10 minutes in warm (not boiling) water is enough. They will finish cooking in the broth.

notes.title: Meat Options
notes.content: You can use all pork, all chicken, or add small shrimp for variety. Leftover rotisserie chicken works well here.

notes.title: Symbolism
notes.content: Pancit is traditionally served at Filipino birthday celebrations to symbolise long life. For this reason, avoid cutting the noodles before serving.
